name: Ectodermal Dysplasia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Hypohidrotic Ectodermal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Reduced or absent sweat gland function leading to hypohidrosis or anhidrosis
Congenital absence of multiple teeth or abnormal tooth morphology
Sparse, thin, or absent scalp and body hair
Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing, saddle nose, and prominent lips
Positive family history consistent with X-linked or autosomal inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (hypohidrosis, hypodontia, hypotrichosis) or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for EDA, EDAR, or EDARADD mutations can confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypohidrosis or anhidrosis due to absent or dysfunctional sweat glands
Hypodontia with conical or peg-shaped teeth
searchTerms: tooth absence and abnormal tooth form

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypotrichosis characterized by sparse, thin scalp and body hair

common.symptomName: Dry, thin skin with decreased sebaceous gland function
Frontal bossing and saddle nose deformity
Heat intolerance due to impaired thermoregulation
Periorbital hyperpigmentation and fine wrinkling around eyes
Delayed eruption of primary and permanent teeth

occasional.symptomName: Recurrent respiratory infections due to mucous gland hypoplasia
Dry mucous membranes including dry eyes and dry mouth
searchTerms: lack of moisture in mouth and eyes

occasional.symptomName: Eczema or atopic dermatitis-like skin changes
Mild developmental delay in some cases
searchTerms: mild delay in learning or development

rare.symptomName: Anhidrotic episodes causing hyperthermia and heat stroke
Corneal opacities secondary to dry eye syndrome
Cardiac anomalies such as congenital heart defects

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in EDA, EDAR, or EDARADD genes
Sweat test showing reduced or absent sweat production
imaging: Dental radiographs showing hypodontia and abnormal tooth morphology
Chest imaging may show recurrent infections or bronchiectasis
genetic: X-linked recessive inheritance most common (EDA gene mutation)
Autosomal dominant and recessive forms linked to EDAR and EDARADD mutations
other: Skin biopsy showing absent or hypoplastic sweat glands

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering skin lesions in neonatal period
X-linked dominant inheritance with male lethality

redFlags: Recurrent hyperthermia episodes due to anhidrosis
Recurrent respiratory infections with risk of bronchiectasis
references: Cluzeau C, Hadj-Rabia S, Jambou M, et al. Clinical and genetic heterogeneity of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia: a comprehensive study of 60 cases. J Med Genet. 2011;48(1):23-31.
Itin PH, Fistarol SK. Ectodermal dysplasias. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2004;131C(1):45-51.
